text.p: Following are the highlights of main stories in Serbian and Montenegrin papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- S E R B I A --
POLITIKA

- Yugoslavia is a factor that has a decisive influence on stability in the Balkans and in southeastern Europe, said ruling Soicialist Party of Serbia (SPS) vice-president and presidential candidate Zoran Lilic in an interview with USA Today.
- Yugoslavia does not lag far behind leading European transition countries, according to a UNICEF study.

- Yugoslav government is pursuing its reform policy and plans to step up its activity in August and September towards an increase of production and exports and return of the country to international organisations, said Yugoslav government secretary general Ljubisa Popovic.
- Opposition Serbian Radical Party (SRS) is dissatisfied with its representation in both state and independent media.

- Yugoslav Defence Minister Pavle Bulatovic pointed to the hidden separatism of the so-called reform wing of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) of Montenegro represented by Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- The cogress of the DPS faction led by Momir Bulatovic expressed strong support to the strengthening of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

- Bosnian Serb constitutional court's ruling to overrule the Bosnian Serb president's decision to disband parliament puts an end to the country's constitutional crisis but not its political one, said parliament speaker Dragan Kalinic.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition Democratic Party (DS) may take part in Serbian elections if the old electoral system dividing Serbia into nine constitutencies is returned, according to party sources.

- Yugoslav constitutional court is not authorised to rule on Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic's appeal on the decision of the Montenegrin constitutional court to strike his presidential candidacy, said member of Serbian constitutional court Slobodan Vucetic.
- The part of the opposition that is boycotting elections is acting solely against the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO), said SPO president Vuk Draskovic.

- There are 250,000 refugees in Yugoslavia who are older than 64 and younger than 18 and fall in the most vulnerable category, according to the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).

- Slovenia to officially protest to international mediator on successionof ex-Yugoslavia over possibile privatisation of former Slovenian firms in Yugoslavia before division of assets of the former federation.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Congress of the Montenegrin Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) faction of Momir Bulatovic means a formal division of the party in two.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA

- Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic met Belgrade mayor and president of Democratic Party Zoran Djindjic in Budva on Sunday. It is in Yugoslavia's interest that reform forces in Montenegro win, said a press release.

- Montenegro's trade deficit in the first seven months this year is $103 million, exports were worth $66 million while imports were $169 million, according to statistics. The average July salary was 900 dinars. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
